answer.railsThatCanServeFromParcelRecordCellThr: None, in the sense the 2026-09-11 ruling means (dereference an atom). All 65 rails are value-copied-only: 26,814,129 value cells, 0 pointers. What CAN be served today is the copied value with its provenance fields - which is what the ruling says a cell is not.
railsThatNeedAtomsMintedFirst: The four envelope rails (maxHeightFt, maxFootprintSqFt, maxLotCoveragePct, maxImperviousCoverPct): the gate is not slated for any of them (maxHeightFtFactServeCutover.ts:9-11), 120 of 378 sampled parcels carry a maxHeightFt value cell, and only 271 of 378 sampled parcels have a buildable-envelope atom at all. Both the pointer AND the atom coverage are missing.

The setback group (setbackFrontFt/SideFt/RearFt/CornerFt + setbackRules): the atom exists for 61.7% of the parcels whose cell carries a value, and disagrees on 30.2% of those where it does. Minting is needed for the second kind of gap (74 of 193 sampled parcels have a cell value and no atom) and adjudication for the first.

zoningDistrict/zoningJurisdictionKey/zoningProvenance: the ONLY rails where the canonical claim already exists for every sampled parcel (zoning-fact 378/378). These three are the rails that can be repointed to the ledger first, ahead of any minting work.
answer.howACachedRenderingWouldKeyToTheCellVers: It cannot today, and this is a schema fact rather than an opinion: parcel_record_cell is (place_key text, rail_key text, cell_state jsonb, updated_at timestamptz) and nothing else - no version column, no pointer column. The only version-ish field is updated_at, a wall-clock stamp, and the cell_state's `vintage` field is the SOURCE's date ('2026-09-15T00:54:11.683Z' on 48209:100226's setback cell), not a content version of the cell. A rendering keyed to 'atom version and vocabulary version' therefore needs the pointer and a content version to exist first; both are P-163's scope, not this lane's.
retirementOrderForTheBake: 1. Land the writer (P-163: pointer + content version in cell_state) - without it there is nothing for a rendering to key to and nothing for the reader to dereference.

2. Repoint the reader that already reads the ledger (LDT's parcelRecordCellRead.ts) to retrieval-api's reader, so the two stop being parallel implementations of the same read. This is the only consumer that already serves a customer from the ledger.

3. Repoint the map's atom-chain adapter (hauska-map atom-chain-to-facets.ts:487-518) - it is the surface the customer actually sees, and it is the one that reads atoms instead of cells, which is why the panel and the MCP disagree today.

4. Retire the bake per rail, not per county, with a divergence test in the overlap: for the setback group the divergence is already visible (cell 30 vs atom 25 in Bastrop) and the test would have to pick a side before it can assert anything.
5. Only after 1-4, retire the legacy derive (legacy-design-tools buildableEnvelope/derive.ts:220).
whereTheProposalConflictsWithThe2026_09_: The ruling says a cell is accounting, 'never a copied value'. On disk, 26,814,129 value cells ARE copied values and none of them is accounting-with-a-pointer. Either the ruling needs a named transition window in which the copied value is permitted while the pointer is absent, or every consumer repoint is blocked behind the writer. RECOMMEND THE OPERATOR RULE: the copied value is permitted ONLY while the pointer is absent, and its presence is itself a measured defect (this instrument reports it), so the number cannot be forgotten.

The ruling says 'one reader in retrieval-api'. There are three, and one of them (LDT's) is the one serving customers today. A lane that builds the retrieval-api reader without a ruled retirement order for LDT's copy adds a fourth diverging producer. RECOMMEND THE OPERATOR RULE the retirement order above, in that order.

The ruling's 'cached rendering keyed to atom version and vocabulary version' has no version to key to in parcel_record_cell. RECOMMEND the operator fold the version column into P-163's scope explicitly, because a rendering cache built today would key to updated_at and be wrong in exactly the silent way this program keeps finding.

disclosures: MISTAKE, DISCLOSED: during reconnaissance one unfiltered probe was launched against the 199 GB atoms table (SELECT ... ORDER BY fetched_at DESC LIMIT 1 with no matching index) and was killed within ~35 s of starting. It read no user data (it read atom body text), it wrote nothing, and it was replaced by a properly indexed point lookup. No other statement in this lane ran without SET statement_timeout and SET default_transaction_read_only=on.
CP1 was filed after the instrument's first draft rather than strictly before it (see CP1.phaseNote); nothing downstream depends on the ordering, and no store write or deploy happened at any point.

The M2 sample's county-level spread is large (setback-rule atoms 0/50 in McLennan, 40/60 in Bastrop). County-level numbers are reported with their own denominators and must not be read as statewide rates.

The 48453 (Travis) sample query took 268 s and 48309 (McLennan) 81 s for the same statement shape: the county place_key prefix range does not cost the same per row in every county. Relevant to anyone who assumes a per-county scan budget.

The 48309 sample was deepened to 50 parcels with a second pass at 25-per-city (the first pass capped at 20 and returned 40 over two city values); the deepening re-ran the same statement with one constant changed, and the final sample file is the deeper one.

hauska-map and LDT are cited at their refs as read (LDT origin/main 62e7349b; hauska-map and the factory tree were read from the checkouts on this machine). No file outside the engine clone was written.
